summary: Settlements stopped because settlement-service's consumer is permanently blocked on a single poison record, orders-3@8841207, which it cannot deserialize ("missing required field 'qty'; schema v1 expected, header says v2") — the mechanism, onset and scope are well established. The onset is tightly correlated with the window's only deployment, order-service v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z: lag began rising and request_rate collapsed at ~07:42Z, with the first deserialization error at 07:42:14Z and explicit "poison message ... partition blocked" retries from 07:44:51Z. The top hypothesis H1 (order-service v2.16.0 emitted a v2-schema record the settlement v1 reader cannot parse) is the best-supported explanation, but confidence is capped at 0.50 because its decisive causal hop — that this specific record was produced by v2.16.0 after 07:40Z, and whether the fault is a malformed producer payload (H1) or a stale v1 consumer reader (H5, 0.42) — rests on record provenance and reader-version data that no available surface exposes. Alternatives H3 (broker reassignment) and H2 (poll-config change) are weakly supported or untestable, and H4 (ledger-db) is excluded by flat telemetry. Outcome: inconclusive, with a safe mitigation and two discriminating checks below.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema change produced a record the settlement consumer cannot deserialize, poisoning partition 3
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service v2.16.0 (deployed 07:40:00Z) changed the OrderExecuted event schema ('qty'->'quantity', added 'venue', schema-version header v2). The first such record landed at orders-3@8841207 ~07:42Z; settlement-service's consumer failed to deserialize it ('missing required field qty', schema v1 expected, header says v2), and because the offset can never be committed it permanently blocks partition 3. No further offsets are consumed, so request_rate collapses to ~0.4 req/s, consumer_lag climbs 603->61605, and CPU stays elevated in the tight retry loop.

causal_chain.claim: order-service v2.16.0 deployed at 07:40:00Z changes the OrderExecuted schema: qty->quantity, +venue, header schema version v2; it is the only deploy in the window
order-service produces the new-schema event to the shared kafka topic, landing on partition orders-3 and reaching settlement-service within ~2 min
settlement-service consumer reads offset orders-3@8841207 with a v1 reader and fails: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)
Failure is not transient: the same offset is retried tens of thousands of times and blocks partition 3
Partition blocked -> no commits/processing -> request_rate collapses ~61->~0.4 req/s and consumer_lag climbs 603->61605
CPU holds ~70% as the retry/deserialize loop spins

assumptions: The poison offset 8841207 was produced by order-service AFTER the 07:40Z deploy (no produced-at timestamp observed; F31/F32/F41 show producer-side and payload surfaces are unavailable).
The record's value actually carries 'quantity'+'venue' under a v2 header (vs. a malformed/legacy value with a mis-set v2 header); unreadable per F32/F41.
order-service is the producer of this record on the orders topic to which settlement-service subscribes (topology not directly proven at record level).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Settlement-service's own stale v1 consumer reader is the owning fault; the producer is healthy and spec-compliant (version skew in the consumer)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The order-service v2.16.0 schema change is a legitimate, backward-incompatible-at-v1 change AND the settlement-service consumer was never upgraded to a v2-aware reader. The fault ORIGINATES in settlement-service's consumer configuration/version skew (its v1 reader), not in the producer. The producer emits well-formed v2 records; only the settlement consumer, still pinned to a v1 schema, chokes and blocks its own partition. Fix belongs to settlement-service (upgrade reader / add schema-registry compatibility), not order-service.

causal_chain.claim: order-service v2.16.0 legitimately begins emitting v2-headered OrderExecuted records at ~07:40Z
settlement-service's consumer reader remains a v1 reader and has not been redeployed/upgraded in the window (only order-service deployed)
The two error patterns on settlement-service are incompatible-schema/poison errors localized to a single consumer's partition
The only other consumer of the orders topic (notification-service) shows NO lag growth, NO deserialize errors, and healthy throughput at onset
Absence of the signal on the other consumer points to consumer-side ownership (settlement's reader) rather than a producer/broker-wide fault
Settlement-consumer partition blocked -> request_rate collapse and lag climb confined to settlement-service

assumptions: notification-service consumes the orders topic but is NOT assigned partition 3 (its clean state could reflect partition coverage, not schema tolerance); partition map is unexposed per F26/F37 gaps.
The producer's v2 payload is well-formed (cannot be read; error text is the only evidence of the mismatch side).
settlement-service's consumer code version at 07:42Z was unchanged/stale (its last deploy was not directly read; bounded only by F1/F23 showing no settlement deploy in the window).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka partition-3 reassignment/leader change stalled the consumer (historical pattern HIST-104/HIST-112)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A broker-side event on the shared kafka cluster (partition reassignment, leader change, rebalance storm as in HIST-112/HIST-104) around 07:42Z stalled settlement-service's consumer group on partition 3, while the schema/config changes are coincidental.

causal_chain.claim: A partition-level reassignment/leader change occurs on orders partition 3 at ~07:42Z
Settlement-service consumer group is left blocked on partition 3, so no offsets are consumed
Lag climbs and request_rate collapses as a result
Historical precedent exists for exactly this pattern

assumptions: A broker event actually occurred at onset (never queried; no broker event surface exists).
A partition-3-only event would leave the poison-offset error as the dominant symptom rather than a distinct rebalance/assignment message.
order-service/notification-service on the same broker would still be healthy under a partition-3-only event (F12/F33/F36 are consistent with this).

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service consumer poll-config change caused a rebalance/stall loop (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 07:35Z settlement-service config change (max.poll.records 500->200, the only config change in the window) caused the consumer to stall or rebalance-loop so nothing processes.

causal_chain.claim: settlement-service max.poll.records changed 500->200 at 07:35Z
Smaller poll batches induce commit/session-timeout or rebalance churn that halts processing
Zero settlements processed and lag climbs

assumptions: A reduced max.poll.records alone can block a partition indefinitely.
No explicit rebalance/session-timeout log exists at INFO level (never checked).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db degradation blocked the consumer; schema/config changes are coincidental
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared ledger-db (used by both order-service and settlement-service) degraded around onset, causing the consumer to block on DB calls so it fetches but cannot commit, growing lag.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db slows at onset
Consumer blocks on ledger-db writes and stops committing
Historical precedent that ledger-db can stall downstream consumers

assumptions: ledger-db had query-latency/lock contention at 07:42Z; every available metric is flat, but it exposes no latency metric so a sub-2-minute blip cannot be fully resolved.
A DB stall would produce a deserialization error and a single repeating poison offset (it would not).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: All four ledger-db metric families that exist (cpu_pct F18, slow_queries_per_min F19, replication_lag_ms F20, connections_active F21) are flat across the 07:15Z-08:30Z window including the 07:41/07:43Z buckets, and settlement-service db_pool_in_use is flat at ~6 with zero restarts (F17). A DB-side block would not produce a deserialization error or a single repeating poison offset (F9, F10/F29). Mechanism mismatch plus zero corroborating telemetry.

facts.statement: Only one deployment occurred across all services in 07:00-09:59Z: order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z (author a.khan, status live, not rolled back), and it changes the OrderExecuted Kafka event schema (rename qty->quantity, add venue, schema version header v2).
The only config change in the window was on settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z by m.das.

settlement-service consumer_lag was flat at baseline (~26-64) through 07:40Z, rose starting 07:42Z (bucket avg 603.29) and climbed to 61605.53 by 09:56Z; lag growth began ~07:42Z, not at the 08:22Z report time.

settlement-service request_rate collapsed at the same instant: ~61-67 req/s through 07:38Z, then ~0.39-0.41 req/s from the 07:42Z bucket onward, consistent with the consumer ceasing to process/commit and with zero settlements processed.

The earliest settlement-service ERROR is at 2026-05-12T07:42:14Z: a deserialization failure 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' — the consumer-side reader expects v1 while the record header declares v2.

The consumer is actively polling and retrying, not idle: from 07:44:51Z onward the same offset is retried indefinitely ('poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked') with attempt counters in the thousands to tens of thousands, so partition 3 cannot advance past that offset.

Across the whole window ERROR traffic is exactly two patterns tied to the single offset 8841207: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted...' x213 and 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207... partition blocked' x196 = 409 ERROR lines, first 07:42:14Z, last 09:58:31Z; no other offsets are named.
settlement-service CPU climbed from a flat ~27-28% baseline to 49.98 avg / 71.68 max in the 07:37Z bucket and held ~70% thereafter, consistent with a tight retry loop rather than a dependency stall.

settlement-service memory_pct (~49-51%), latency_p99_ms (~233-243 ms), error_rate (~0.21% HTTP 5xx), and db_pool_in_use (~6) are all flat across onset, and restarts is 0 in every bucket 07:15Z-09:49Z — no memory ramp, no latency degradation, no connection-pool exhaustion and no pod crash-loop.

ledger-db shows no degradation coinciding with the stall: cpu_pct flat ~30%, slow_queries_per_min flat (07:41Z=1.04, 07:43Z=1.12), replication_lag_ms flat (~40 ms), and connections_active flat (~62), so no measured DB-side event at or before onset.

order-service (on the same broker) shows no degradation: only 1 WARN in 07:30-09:59Z and it does not expose consumer_lag, suggesting the fault is specific to settlement-service's consumption of the orders topic rather than a broker-wide outage.
In 07:30-07:45Z no config change occurred on kafka (count 0) and no deployment occurred on any other service in 07:30-08:30Z besides order-service v2.16.0.

notification-service is the ONLY other queue-consume consumer of kafka besides settlement-service; it shows no lag growth (flat ~40-70 messages through 09:55Z), zero deserialization/schema errors, flat request_rate ~147 req/s and flat cpu_pct ~25% throughout.
notification-service had zero deployments and zero config changes in 07:00-09:59Z, so its consumer behaviour was not altered by any deploy/config in the window.

The only place offset 8841207 appears in settlement-service logs is ERROR-level (409 lines, zero INFO); no payload dump, no schema header value beyond the error text, and no produced-at timestamp is logged for the poison record.

Producer-side and record-metadata surfaces do not exist anywhere queried: order-service log searches for 'schema', 'quantity', 'OrderExecuted', 'produced' and '8841207' all returned 0 matches; kafka metrics are limited to [cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions] with no record_metadata/producer_id; kafka logs are empty; settlement-service exposes no schema_version or record_timestamp metric.

assumptions: The poison offset 8841207 was produced by order-service AFTER the 07:40Z deploy; no produced-at timestamp was observed on any surface (F31/F32/F41).
The record's value actually carries 'quantity'+'venue' under a v2 header rather than a malformed/legacy value with a mis-set v2 header; the raw payload is unreadable (F32/F41).

recommended_actions.action: Unblock the consumer without waiting for root-cause attribution: skip/park the poison offset orders-3@8841207 for the settlement-service consumer group (offset advance / dead-letter the record), so partition 3 can resume. This is the fastest path to restoring settlements.
recommended_actions.rationale: The partition is provably blocked on one offset and cannot advance (F10/F11/F29/F30); moving past it removes the outage regardless of whether the fault is producer- or consumer-side.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back order-service v2.16.0 on its own as the first action; if a rollback is considered, verify with the order-service owners first, because the v2 schema change is the leading trigger but the fault could equally be the stale v1 reader (H5).
recommended_actions.rationale: Both H1 (0.50) and H5 (0.42) depend on the same v2 schema change; H5 fixes ownership to settlement-service. A unilateral rollback could be the wrong service change.

recommended_actions.action: Discriminate H1 vs H5 by fetching the raw value of orders-3@8841207 (and its schema-version header) from the Kafka topic/consumer-group tooling, and the settlement-service consumer image version / schema-registry compatibility setting in effect at 07:42Z.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the single decisive check: if the payload carries 'quantity'+'venue' under a v2 header while settlement-service runs a v1 reader, ownership moves to settlement-service (H5); if the producer emitted a malformed or legacy payload with a v2 header, H1 stands. Neither surface was reachable in the investigation (F31/F32/F38/F39/F40/F41).

recommended_actions.action: Add a schema-compatibility guard on both sides: order-service should register/validate the OrderExecuted v2 schema in the schema registry with a backward-compatibility check before deploy, and settlement-service should add a dead-letter path plus a schema-registry-aware deserializer so no single record can block a partition.
recommended_actions.rationale: The outage mechanism is a permanent offset block on one undeserializable record (F10/F29); DLQ + schema-registry-aware deserialization makes the failure mode non-blocking.

recommended_actions.action: Verify the fix on two independent metrics: settlement-service consumer_lag returning to the ~26-64 baseline and request_rate recovering from ~0.4 req/s to ~61-67 req/s.
recommended_actions.rationale: These two metrics define the onset (F7/F8) and are the fastest objective recovery signal.

recommended_actions.action: If the raw record shows the fault is producer-side malformed output rather than consumer version skew, gate v2.16.0 and roll it back or patch it; if it shows consumer-side v1 skew, upgrade settlement-service's reader instead and leave the producer.
recommended_actions.rationale: Ownership fork is the unresolved discriminator between the two live hypotheses (H1/H5); the action depends on the record-level check above.

recommended_actions.action: If the record-level check is also inconclusive, close out H3 by querying Kafka broker/consumer-group state for 'orders' (partition 3 reassignment/leader-change/rebalance history) in 07:30-08:30Z. H3 is low-probability (0.05) but untestable with the current tool set and shares the historical pattern HIST-104/HIST-112.
recommended_actions.rationale: H3's exclusion rests on the broker never being queried, not on a negative finding (F24 shows no kafka config change; F12/F33/F36 show no topic-wide impact). Confirming no broker event occurred closes the loop.

recommended_actions.action: Prevent recurrence of the schema-compatibility class: enforce a schema-registry compatibility contract in CI for both order-service and settlement-service, add per-consumer consumer_lag alerts on the orders topic, and document the producer-consumer ownership of the OrderExecuted schema.
recommended_actions.rationale: The window had a legitimate backward-incompatible-at-v1 deploy and a consumer that failed to advance; a compatibility gate plus lag alerting would have caught the mismatch at deploy time and given settlement-service advance warning.

recommended_actions.action: Add a nonexistent-resolution log/metric surface for record provenance (producer id/version, produced_at, raw payload one-line dump) at ERROR level in consumers so future poison-record incidents are attributable without log archaeology.
recommended_actions.rationale: The investigation could not read the poison record's provenance from any surface (F31/F32/F38/F39/F40/F41), which is precisely what left the outcome inconclusive.

recommended_actions.action: Reconsider the settlement-service consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 change (07:35Z) after the incident is resolved; it is weakly implicated (H2, 0.03) and is a reversible config change that was not shown to help.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 is contradicted by a single-offset poison mechanism and flat p99/pool/restarts, but the config change is the reporter's stated suspicion and the only change on the affected service (F2/F15/F17).

data_gaps: No Kafka broker, topic or consumer-group state was queryable: broker/partition reassignment, leader change, rebalance history and consumer-group assignment are all unavailable, so H3 cannot be confirmed or excluded (F24 only shows no kafka config change; F12/F33/F36 show no topic-wide impact).

The poison record's provenance is not obtainable: producer id/version and produced_at are absent from every queried surface (order-service log searches returned 0 matches; kafka has no record_metadata/producer_id metric; kafka logs are empty; settlement-service exposes no schema_version/record_timestamp metric).

The raw value of orders-3@8841207 (actual field names 'qty' vs 'quantity', presence of 'venue', and the schema-version header value beyond the error text) and the running reader's schema version could not be read, so the H1 vs H5 ownership fork cannot be resolved.

No runtime telemetry was obtained for notification-service (the only other orders consumer) — only its flat lag, flat request_rate/cpu and absence of errors, and only zero config/deployment changes. Whether it is genuinely schema-tolerant or simply not assigned partition 3 is unknown because the per-consumer partition map is not exposed.
settlement-service's last deployment timestamp was not read, so its v1 reader could not be bounded as stale-but-legitimate versus actively broken.

ledger-db exposes no query-latency or lock/wait metric and no bucket boundary (07:41Z/07:43Z) shows deviation, but metric buckets are 120s, so a sub-2-minute ledger-db blip exactly at onset cannot be fully excluded.

No JVM/GC or per-dependency downstream latency metrics exist in settlement-service, so whether the CPU rise is retry-loop-driven versus GC-driven is inferred rather than measured (memory_pct is flat).
Only WARN/ERROR levels were examined for settlement-service; a rebalance or poll-timeout message at INFO level would not have been seen.
The 07:42Z onset bucket is a 120s aggregate, so the exact sub-minute rollover was not resolved and the lag-vs-first-error ordering is only bounded to ~2 minutes.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Reading the raw value of orders-3@8841207: if it carries 'quantity' + 'venue' under a v2 header, this confirms the v2-schema trigger and points to consumer-side version skew (H5); if the payload is malformed or legacy with a v2 header, H1's producer-side attribution is strengthened.
Any record metadata showing the poison record's produced_at timestamp is after 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z, which would lock H1 to the order-service v2.16.0 deployment.
Evidence that settlement-service already ran a v2-aware reader at 07:42Z (e.g. its last deploy/schema-registry config), which would shift ownership to order-service and break the H5 mechanism.

A Kafka broker/consumer-group event on partition 3 of the orders topic coinciding with 07:42Z (partition reassignment, leader change, or rebalance storm), which would revive H3 and make the schema/poison record coincidental.

Proof that notification-service consumes partition 3 of the orders topic yet stayed healthy, which would rule out a topic-wide producer/payload fault and strongly confirm the consumer-side (H5) reading.
Evidence that the 07:35Z max.poll.records change or a Kafka session-timeout/rebalance loop produced the same poison-offset signature, which would reorder H2 upward.
Discovery of a ledger-db latency/lock spike shorter than the 120s metric bucket at exactly 07:42Z, which would partially revive H4.

No deployment occurred on any other service in 07:30-08:30Z; the only one is order-service v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z (status live, not rolled back). This bounds the config/deploy-driven rebalance question: nothing was deployed to a broker or a second consumer in the window.
No config change occurred on kafka in 07:30-07:45Z (scope kafka returned count 0), so there is no evidence of a broker-side config/flag action coincident with the 07:42Z onset.

Topology of the shared kafka: only two queue-consume edges exist on kafka -- settlement-service and notification-service. Therefore notification-service is the ONLY other consumer of the orders topic that would experience lag/deserialization errors if the poison event affected all consumers.

notification-service had zero deployments (scope notification-service) and zero config changes in 07:00-09:59Z, so its consumer behaviour was not altered by any deploy/config in this incident window. I could not query its lag/deserialization metrics directly (no tool exposed them and budget ran out), so its runtime health at 07:42Z is NOT established.

Historical precedent for the rebalance hypothesis remains only a lead: HIST-112 'Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment' and HIST-104 'notification-service lag after Kafka broker rebalance' both have root cause 'Partition reassignment', but the incident repo records no broker event for the current case and match_score is low (3 and 2 in this search).

findings.statement: The settlement-service ERROR log identifies the poison record by exact coordinates orders-3@8841207 (topic 'orders', partition 3, offset 8841207) and states the consumer-side deserialization failure is 'missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'. This means the reader is a v1 schema reader (expecting 'qty') while the record's schema-version header declares v2 — the failure is the header/value version mismatch on this specific record, first seen 2026-05-12T07:42:14Z.

findings.statement: The same offset 8841207 is retried indefinitely as a poison message and blocks partition 3: 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked' from 07:44:51Z onward, with attempt counters in the thousands to tens of thousands (92490, 25391, 56347, 14422, 74563, ...). The partition cannot advance past that offset, which explains zero settlements processed and the growing lag.

findings.statement: Across the whole window the ERROR traffic is exactly two patterns tied to the single offset 8841207: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted...' x213 and 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207... partition blocked' x196 = 409 ERROR lines, first 07:42:14Z, last 09:58:31Z. Only one poison offset exists in the observed data, and no other offsets are named.

order-service logs contain NO record of the event/produce side for this window: queries in order-service for 'schema' (tc-030), 'quantity' (tc-031), 'OrderExecuted' (tc-038), 'produced' (tc-039) and '8841207' (tc-040) all returned total_matched=0 over 04:00-09:59Z. No record-metadata / raw-payload surface is available anywhere I queried: settlement-service logs for 'payload' returned total_matched=0 (tc-043), and the settlement-service '8841207' INFO query returned only ERROR-level lines with no payload dump (tc-042). The queries for kafka 'producer' metadata and for the 'venue' field were not executed (tool-call budget exhausted), so producer-id/version, produced-at, and the presence/absence of a 'venue' field are unresolved.

notification-service consumer_lag shows NO lag growth across 07:15Z-08:30Z: it oscillates in a flat baseline band of roughly 40-70 messages (min 18.27, max 94.61, mean 59.96) with no upward trend at or after the 07:42Z onset — pre-onset buckets 07:35Z avg 67.44 and 07:39Z avg 64.17 vs post-onset 07:43Z avg 57.52 and 07:47Z avg 59.73. This is the flat baseline pattern, in stark contrast to settlement-service's climb to 61605.53.

notification-service consumer_lag stays flat for the whole incident through 09:55Z (08:30Z-09:55Z buckets avg 52.31-68.19, min 21.96, max 94.98, mean 61.2) — no sustained climb 2.5 hours after onset. The lag-growth symptom is confined to settlement-service.

notification-service shows NO deserialization or schema error signature at any level 07:15Z-09:59Z: the 'deserialize' filter returned total_matched=0 (tc-046), the ERROR-level query for 07:15Z-08:30Z returned total_matched=0 (tc-045), and the only WARN in 07:15Z-09:59Z is a single unrelated 'clock drift 38ms detected, resyncing with NTP' at 08:39:18Z. findings.statement: notification-service is functionally healthy at onset on two independent metrics besides lag: request_rate is flat at ~147 req/s throughout (07:15Z-08:27Z avg 143.31-150.41, mean 147.4, min 133.71, max 166.73) with no collapse at 07:42Z — unlike settlement-service whose request_rate fell to ~0.4 req/s; and cpu_pct is flat at ~25% (mean 24.98, min 23.09, max 27.46) the entire window. notification-service never stopped processing.

notification-service (the ONLY other consumer of the orders topic on the shared kafka, per F25) shows neither the lag growth nor the identical deserialization signature that settlement-service shows. A record-level schema/poison event on the shared topic would poison every consumer of that partition; a broker/producer-side fault affecting settlement-service's partition 3 would also hit notification-service (also on kafka). Its clean state therefore points away from a topic-wide producer/broker fault and toward something specific to settlement-service's consumer (its v1 schema reader) — i.e. consumer-side ownership.

No record-metadata / payload provenance metric surface exists on kafka: explicit queries for metrics 'record_metadata' (tc-047) and 'producer_id' (tc-048) both returned not_found, and each error enumerated kafka's complete available_metrics as exactly [cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions]. There is therefore no kafka metric that can carry producer id/version or produced-at timestamp.

No schema-version-header or record-timestamp metric surface exists on settlement-service: queries for 'schema_version' (tc-049) and 'record_timestamp' (tc-050) both returned not_found, and the error enumerated settlement-service's complete available_metrics as exactly [consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts]. None of these can yield the record's schema-version header value or produced-at timestamp.

kafka exposes no logs at all over 04:00-09:59Z: 'producer' returned total_matched=0 (tc-051), 'venue' returned total_matched=0 (tc-052), and 'schema' returned total_matched=0 (tc-058). So the broker side cannot supply the record's producer metadata, 'venue' value, or any raw payload — there is no kafka log surface to read.

The only place offset 8841207 appears in settlement-service logs is ERROR-level: an INFO-level query for '8841207' (tc-057) returned total_matched=409, counts_by_level {"ERROR": 409} — i.e. zero INFO lines. No payload dump, no schema header value beyond the error text, and no produced-at timestamp is logged for the poison record; the sole provenance facts are coordinates orders-3@8841207 and the message text 'schema v1 expected, header says v2'.
